intro: Training is how a neural network goes from random guesses to useful predictions. This episode covers parameters, forward pass, loss, backpropagation, gradient descent, self-supervised learning, and why overfitting is the opposite of good generalization.

sections.heading: Trained vs untrained networks
sections.definition: An untrained neural network is like a newborn baby's brain — random parameters, random outputs. A trained network is like an adult who practiced a skill for years. Poor training still produces bad, near-random generations.
points: Inferencing = using a trained model; training = teaching it first
Transformers sit on top of a trained neural network
Learning = adjusting parameters so future predictions improve
The model starts by guessing, measures mistakes, then adjusts

sections.heading: Parameters = learned knobs
sections.definition: Parameters are a huge collection of adjustable numbers (weights and biases) inside the network. At creation they are random; during training they are tuned so the model recognizes patterns and predicts better.
points: Think DJ knobs: model = sound box, parameters = dials you tune
Weights = how important an input is; biases = offsets for decisions
GPT-3 has ~175 billion parameters; newer models have trillions
Knowledge is encoded as patterns across parameters — not stored like human memory
Token embeddings are also parameters that get adjusted during training

sections.heading: Forward pass → Loss → Backpropagation
sections.definition: Forward pass: input flows through layers to produce a prediction. Loss: a number measuring how wrong the prediction is. Backpropagation: travel backward to compute how each parameter affected that loss.
points: Example: 'The sky is ___' predicting 'banana' = high loss; 'blue' = low loss
Correct prediction ⇒ small loss; very wrong ⇒ large loss
Backpropagation calculates gradients — it does not itself update weights
An optimizer then uses gradients to adjust parameters

sections.heading: Gradient descent & optimizers
sections.definition: Gradient descent iteratively walks downhill on the loss surface — opposite to the gradient — to reduce error. Core pieces: loss function, gradient, and learning rate.
points: Batch GD: use entire dataset before one update — accurate but slow
SGD: update after one example — fast but noisy path
Mini-batch GD: small groups (e.g. 32) — industry standard balance
Training loop: sample → forward → loss → backprop → optimize → repeat

sections.heading: Self-supervised learning & training terms
sections.definition: LLMs mostly learn by self-supervised learning: hide parts of raw data and predict them — no human labels needed. Dataset, batch, training step, and epoch describe how that work is organized.
points: Self-supervised: predict next word / fill missing pieces from unlabeled text
Dataset = all training data; Batch = group processed together on GPU
Training step = one optimization update
Epoch = one full pass through the entire dataset
Training needs huge compute/GPUs because the loop runs many times

sections.heading: Training vs inference, generalization, overfitting
sections.definition: Training teaches the model; inference uses it for new answers. Good learning generalizes to unseen examples. Overfitting memorizes training data and fails on new cases.
points: Training = expensive forward+backward learning; inference = cheaper prediction
Generalization = apply learned patterns beyond exact training examples
Overfitting = great on training data, weak on new data
Distributed training splits work across many GPUs/nodes for scale
